# docs/memory/core/

<!-- Generated by php tools/memory_index.php, except the key rules between the two marker lines, which are written by hand. -->

Code rules, file layout, translation, JavaScript twins and bundles, roles and access, security, api.php, request parameters.

## Key rules

<!-- key-rules:start -->
- Start every screen with `validate_user()` and its `validate_area_access()` gate; Designer (1) is above Manager (2), and a hidden button is no access check (`access-control-and-roles.md`).
- Teach a new role-3 right to every role-3 ladder file: `welcome.php`, `get_page.php`, `includes/fn/content.php`, `set_password.php`, `reset_password.php` (`permission-columns.md`).
- Print `get_token_field()` in every form that changes data and check it with `validate_token_field()` before writing; a JSON endpoint checks the token itself (`security-helpers-and-secret-storage.md`).
- Escape every value printed into HTML with `h()`, `lang()` `{var:N}` values included; give `h()` a raw `&` in query strings; wrap `_sdT()` in `esc()` (`output-escaping.md`).
- Make a JSON endpoint refuse in JSON with a status (`validate_area_access()`, `validate_token_field()` print HTML); `api.php` reads only a JSON body (`json-endpoint-rules.md`).
- Add an `api.php` action as a `pg_panel_actions()` row; unlisted names hit the session + role <= 1 gate, so a role 2/3 action is `exempt` (its handler checks session, token, role) or `any_role` (`panel-action-table.md`).
- Keep a secret config value as one encrypted blob decrypted where used: never a constant, never hashed if it must be read back, never shown back on a settings screen (a new field is drawn empty) (`security-helpers-and-secret-storage.md`).
- Build a module's paths from `PG_FUNCTIONS_DIR`, not `__DIR__`, and start every include with its loader's gate constant (`functions-php-split-rules.md`, `file-placement-rules.md`).
<!-- key-rules:end -->

## Files

- `INDEX.md` lists the 172 files of this folder, one line each: search it rather than read it whole, then open only the files that match.
- `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/core/INDEX.md`; across every folder: `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/*/INDEX.md`.
